name: Concrete
subtitle: Durable, large-scale pieces
volumeHint: Fill your mould with water and weigh it. Its grams are the volume in ml. For odd shapes, use the water-displacement method: submerge the master in a known volume of water and measure the rise.

variants.name: Fine craft mix
variants.useCase: Coasters, candle vessels, small pots, detailed pieces — smooth finish, no visible aggregate. For an even smoother surface increase cement to 1.5:1 ratio (test first).
variants.sourceNote: Derived from absolute-volume method: 1:2 cement:sand, w/c 0.45, quartz sand SG 2.65, Portland cement SG 3.15, ~2% air. Per 1 kg cement: 317.5 + 754.7 + 450 = 1522 cm³ ÷ 0.98 = 1553 cm³; 3450 g total → 2.22 g/ml. Source: research report cross-referencing Davis Colors, ASTM, and standard mix design. Absolute-volume method per ACI/standard mix design. Specific gravities: Portland cement 3.15, quartz sand/gravel 2.65, water 1.0. ~2% entrapped air for hand-mixed cast.

pourable.label: Pourable
pourable.note: Flows easily into detailed moulds. Slightly weaker — avoid over-watering.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.note: Good workability and strength. Default for most craft pieces.

stiff.label: Stiff
stiff.note: Stronger and denser. Needs vibration to settle. Best for simple open shapes.

additives.name: Iron oxide pigment
additives.note: 1–5% of cement weight is typical; maximum 10% of cement weight (ASTM C979, Davis Colors). Mix dry into the cement before adding other dry ingredients. More than 10% weakens the mix. Cement weight only — not total mix weight.

additives.name: Plasticiser
additives.note: Reduces the water needed by the percentage you set. The water figure on the card updates automatically. Do not add extra water on top.

variants.demouldTime: 24 h minimum. Wait 48–72 h for full handling strength. Full cure at 28 days.
tips: Mix dry ingredients (cement, sand, pigment if using) together first until evenly coloured
Add water gradually — use the least amount that still lets the mix flow into the mould
Tap and vibrate the mould for at least 1–2 minutes to bring air bubbles to the surface
A wet-mud-pie or firm brownie-batter consistency is about right
Cover with plastic wrap while curing to slow drying and reduce cracking
Do not cure in direct sun, wind or temperatures above 30°C
safety: Wear gloves — wet cement is alkaline and will dry out and irritate skin
Wear a dust mask when handling dry cement powder
Not food safe. Seal before use as a planter or vessel.

variants.name: General casting mix
variants.useCase: Planters, tiles, outdoor pieces — more aggregate look, better strength in bulk
variants.sourceNote: Derived from absolute-volume method: 1:2:3 cement:sand:gravel, w/c 0.5, quartz SG 2.65, Portland cement SG 3.15, ~2% air. Density 2.36 g/ml. Source: research report. Absolute-volume method per ACI/standard mix design. Specific gravities: Portland cement 3.15, quartz sand/gravel 2.65, water 1.0. ~2% entrapped air for hand-mixed cast.

pourable.label: Pourable
pourable.note: Easier to fill around aggregate. Vibrate well.

stiff.label: Stiff
stiff.note: Strongest option. Needs thorough vibration — aggregate traps more air.

additives.name: Iron oxide pigment
additives.note: 1–5% of cement weight is typical; maximum 10% of cement weight (ASTM C979, Davis Colors). Mix dry into the cement before adding other dry ingredients. More than 10% weakens the mix. Cement weight only — not total mix weight.

additives.name: Plasticiser
additives.note: Reduces the water needed by the percentage you set. The water figure on the card updates automatically. Do not add extra water on top.

variants.demouldTime: 24–48 h minimum. Full handling strength at 72 h. Full cure at 28 days.
tips: Mix dry ingredients first: cement, sand, aggregate, and pigment if using
Add water gradually — aggregate makes the mix feel drier than it is, so resist adding too much
Vibrate for longer than a fine mix — gravel traps air and takes more time to release bubbles
For a more mottled, rough concrete look, vibrate less
safety: Wear gloves — wet cement is alkaline
Wear a dust mask when handling dry cement powder
Not food safe. Seal for outdoor or planter use.
